name: Linear Hypopigmentation and Craniofacial Asymmetry with Acral, Ocular and Brain Anomalies
aliases: Linear Hypopigmentation Syndrome with Craniofacial and Neurological Anomalies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Linear Hypopigmentation and Craniofacial Asymmetry Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of linear hypopigmented skin lesions following Blaschko lines
Unilateral craniofacial asymmetry including hemifacial microsomia or hypoplasia
Congenital acral malformations such as syndactyly or brachydactyly
Ocular abnormalities including microphthalmia, coloboma, or strabismus
Structural brain anomalies detected by neuroimaging such as cortical dysplasia or ventriculomegaly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: linear hypopigmentation, craniofacial asymmetry, and acral anomalies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Additional minor criteria such as ocular or brain anomalies support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Linear hypopigmented skin lesions following Blaschko lines
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic hypopigmentation pattern is diagnostic hallmark
searchTerms: light-colored skin lines following body patterns
linear pale skin patches along Blaschko lines

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral craniofacial asymmetry with hemifacial microsomia
pathognomonic.notes: Facial asymmetry typically evident at birth or early infancy
searchTerms: unequal face size on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital acral malformations including syndactyly or brachydactyly
searchTerms: abnormal hand or foot development at birth
abnormal eye shape or holes in eye structures

common.notes: Mild to moderate cognitive impairment reported
Structural brain abnormality contributing to neurological symptoms
searchTerms: cortical brain abnormalities seen on imaging

occasional.notes: Enlarged cerebral ventricles detected by MRI

searchTerms: drooping on one side of face
holes or defects in heart walls

imaging: MRI brain showing cortical dysplasia and ventriculomegaly
CT or MRI of craniofacial bones showing asymmetry
other: Clinical observation of linear hypopigmentation along Blaschko lines
Detailed ophthalmological and neurological assessments recommended

distinguishingFeatures: Hypopigmentation with neurological abnormalities but lacks consistent craniofacial asymmetry
Linear skin hypoplasia with skeletal and ocular anomalies but includes papillomas and fat herniation

redFlags: Onset of seizures or status epilepticus
